precepts.text: And Tychicus have I sent to Ephesus. Ephesus is right there next to Colosse; the same messengers served that whole region.
precepts.point: What thou seest, write in a book, and send it unto the seven churches which are in Asia: Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamos, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea. Laodicea was right there next to Colosse. On the map, Philadelphia and Sardis are all right there by Colosse as well.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
John is told, “What thou seest, write in a book, and send it unto the seven churches which are in Asia”, and the first of them is Ephesus. Paul writes to Timothy, “And Tychicus have I sent to Ephesus.”

That same Tychicus was sent to Colosse. In Colossians 4, “All my state shall Tychicus declare unto you, who is a beloved brother, and a faithful minister and fellowservant in the Lord: Whom I have sent unto you for the same purpose, that he might know your estate, and comfort your hearts”, together “With Onesimus, a faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you.”

Ephesus is right there next to Colosse. The same messengers served that whole region, going between the churches of Asia. So the Colossians were not off by themselves: they were part of that same body of churches in Asia that Christ sent his word to in Revelation.

precepts.text: Bring the books: the books meaning the books of Isaiah, the books of Jeremiah, the books of Micah. It's not talking about books about how to braid your hair. But especially the parchments: parchments are writing papers. So he would read the Old Testament books and base his epistles on those writings.
precepts.point: If heaven above can be measured, and the foundations of the earth searched out beneath, I will also cast off all the seed of Israel. Nobody can measure heaven or search out all the places of the earth. So this is where Paul was getting it from.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Paul writes to Timothy: “The cloke that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments.” The books means the books of Isaiah, the books of Jeremiah, the books of Micah. It is not talking about books about how to braid your hair.

“but especially the parchments”: parchments are writing papers. Paul would read the Old Testament books and base his epistles on those writings. That is why Hebrews 8 carries the new covenant word for word out of Jeremiah 31: Paul was reading Jeremiah and writing from it.

So the New Testament does not replace the Old; it is built on it. When Jeremiah says the new covenant is with the house of Israel and the house of Judah, and that the seed of Israel will not cease from being a nation while the sun, moon and stars stand, Paul was taking that from the prophets he carried with him. The church did not get a new covenant of its own; Paul was teaching Israel's covenant out of Israel's books.

precepts.text: Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day.
precepts.point: For it is not a light thing to do wickedly against the laws of God. Sometimes we take the laws of the Most High for granted with the mentality, I can sin and God won't do nothing.
precepts.why:
Paul said a man is not crowned “except he strive lawfully.” What does he mean by crowned? He tells it in the same book: “Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.”

The crown is not a rank a man buys or cheats his way into, like Jason bribing the king for the high priesthood. It is a crown of righteousness laid up by the Lord, the righteous judge, and given at that day to those who strove lawfully and love his appearing.

So the brother who wants to be moved up, to be an officer, a captain, a deacon, must remember whose crown he is striving for. Jason got the rule in his hand for a time, but the writer of Maccabees still calls him “that ungodly wretch, and no high priest.”

precepts.text: The cloke that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments. The parchments are the writing papers he wrote his epistles on; the books are the books of Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel. Paul was always studying. He was a man of study; he did not stop.
precepts.point: As ye have been taught: some of the leadership from the old school went off, and the doctrine became that everything they taught was wrong, so throw it away and go back to Christianity. Did King Solomon go off? Do we rip out the book of Proverbs? Did King David go off? Do we rip out the book of Psalms? Men make mistakes, men do fall, but when they were in their prime they were teaching properly. You do not throw the baby away with the bath water.
precepts.why:
To be “Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith,” you have to study, and Paul is the example. “The cloke that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments.”

The parchments are the writing papers he wrote his epistles on; he was going to be writing a lot of letters. The books are the books of Isaiah, Jeremiah and Ezekiel. Even in prison, Paul wanted his books.

Paul was always studying. He was a man of study, and he did not stop. We do four chapters a day; that is low level, but we have to start low level so we can get to a big level. Being rooted in Christ means never putting the books down.

precepts.text: The Lord stood with me and strengthened me. You get weak, need counsel, need to vent; a leader is there to strengthen you.
precepts.point: Think of the faith the Bishop had to have for the truth to be where it is. The impact reaches beyond the purple and gold: outsiders email to donate to the booster club, and every camp watches IUIC at 6 on Saturday night whatever time they teach themselves.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
“Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known”. The Lord stood with Paul and strengthened him, so that the preaching might go forth by him.

That is our job: we must strengthen one another. You get weak at different times. You need counsel. You need some exhortation. You have to vent sometimes. And it is your job as a leader to be there to strengthen each other, as the Lord stood with Paul.

So those who have the rule over you and speak the word of God unto you are there to strengthen you, and when you are strengthened, you follow their faith and do the same for those around you.

precepts.text: Sown on stony ground: they hear the word and receive it with gladness, I am an Israelite, but have no root, no study, sports and porn first and Bible last, and endure but for a time; when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word's sake, immediately they are offended. Satan asks to test you where you are weak, and the brother struggling with a proclivity who goes to the gym at two in the morning finds two men in the shower inviting him in; stay out of the gym and do calisthenics at home. Sown among thorns: the cares of this world, the deceitfulness of riches, and the lust of other things, the thing in you that nobody else knows but God, Satan, and you, choke the word.
precepts.point: Matthew 24:10: then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another. In 2018 brothers were dropping like flies, brothers we broke bread with who stayed in our homes, offended at the gospel and betraying it. Some tried to start Israelite congregations and fell overnight; God will not bless your hands after so much evil to your brothers and sisters.
precepts.why:
“For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world.” Demas traveled with Paul and warred with Paul, and he forsook Paul. He saw the looseness of the women: Paul, I’ve got to go, my man, I can’t roll with you no more, I got needs. He let that overcome him. Crescens left for Galatia, Titus for Dalmatia. Mark shows what happened to Paul’s companions, men who were strong in the Lord and in the power of his might. Those guys are some of you guys.

“And these are they likewise which are sown on stony ground; who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with gladness.” I’m an Israelite, we got history, oh I love it. “And have no root in themselves, and so endure but for a time.” No root: I don’t study, I don’t addict myself to the ministry, I like my sports, I like my porn, the Bible comes last. So you only endure this gospel for a time.

“afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word’s sake, immediately they are offended.” Offended, and you leave. Affliction is things that happen to you; persecution is what happens to you for the word’s sake, because you stand strong in this Bible. That is why Paul told Timothy not to be ashamed of his affliction, to suffer in it with him and stir up the gift within him. Christ lets us know some of us are going to leave this truth because of affliction.

And Satan will test. He asks the Lord, can I test him? Can I test her? The brother with a proclivity for the male gender went to the gym at two in the morning, where the freaks come out at night, found two men in the shower, stood there five whole minutes, and they invited him to join in. If you are struggling, stay out of the gym; do calisthenics at your house. You are trying to fight a spirit; don’t go around spirits like that.

“And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word, And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.” The cares of this world and the deceitfulness of riches, a piece of the American pie, may not be your thing. But the lust of other things is anything in you that nobody else knows. You may hide it very well, but God knows it is there, Satan knows it is there, and you do too. Satan is not tempting you with a pork chop. He looks into your soul, sees what you are battling with, and asks to tempt you right there.

That is what took Demas, Crescens and Titus, and it is what Paul went through with Alexander the coppersmith, who was in the ministry and turned against it, “for he hath greatly withstood our words.” We have seen the same: men in the gospel who went online to try to tear this down. “At my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me.” Christ already prophesied it: “And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.” In 2018 brothers were dropping like flies, brothers and sisters we broke bread with, who stayed in our homes and knew our families, offended at the gospel and betraying it. Some tried to start Israelite congregations and fell overnight. God is not going to bless your hands after you did so much evil to your brothers and sisters.

precepts.text: Not giving heed to Jewish fables and commandments of men.
precepts.point: Titus warns against Jewish fables and the commandments of men that turn from the truth.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
“And they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables.” That is why people have left the truth of the word of God to follow fables. Christmas is a fable. All of those are fables, meaning lies, story-told lies, with symbolic meanings in the stories: Santa Claus and his blackened helper, Santa with his horse in the Netherlands and his flying reindeer here, Rudolph and the fairy dust. Our people have celebrated this foolishness for a long time.

Titus gives the warning: “Not giving heed to Jewish fables, and commandments of men, that turn from the truth.” Don’t give heed to them. Christmas and all these things are commandments of men, and they turn you from the truth.

That is why you have people online saying it is not wrong to celebrate Christmas, it is in your heart, it is how you feel, and all that crap. It is turning you from the truth of God. Some try to figure it out: we agree his birthday is not December 25th, so we can make up another day. That is what they do, but it always comes back to December 25th. It is still a fable and a commandment of men, and Paul told Timothy the people would turn away their ears from the truth to follow it.

precepts.text: Christ kept the feast of dedication in winter, not a December birthday.
precepts.point: Titus warns against Jewish fables and the commandments of men that turn from the truth.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
There is a winter holiday that Christ kept: “And it was at Jerusalem the feast of the dedication, and it was winter.” Read on: “And Jesus walked in the temple in Solomon’s porch.” The feast of dedication is celebrated in the winter, and Christ was there at the feast in the wintertime.

So the holiday of the winter that Christ kept was the feast of dedication, not a December birthday. Christmas, December 25th and the birthday of Christ are fables and commandments of men, and people have turned their ears from the truth to follow them.

The same goes for the new year. The new year is in the spring, not the winter. Abib, or Aviv, means spring: the season when the young, tender barley ears first appear, marking the start of the religious new year around March or April in the Gregorian calendar, the time of the Passover and the firstfruits offering, signifying renewal and freedom from Egypt. They celebrate the new year in the winter. And if you see Israelite groups keeping Passover in February, or July, or June, there is something wrong. The truth is in the scriptures; the winter birthday and the winter new year are the fables they turned to.

precepts.text: Paul could say, I have fought a good fight, because he knew a crown of righteousness was laid up for him; that is the fight Israel is in now.
precepts.point: The Most High strengthens nations and weakens nations, and moves peoples in and out of lands to fulfil his word. In this last battle Israel cannot lose so long as we keep the commandments, have faith in Christ, and endure to the end; but if we stay in sin, we die with the heathen.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

precepts.why:
Jephthah said “whomsoever the Lord our God shall drive out from before us, them will we possess”: we will possess whatever the Most High gives us, and we are not backing down from anybody. That is the fight Israel is in now. Paul could say, “I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith”, because he knew “there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day”. The same righteous Judge Jephthah called on to judge between Israel and Ammon gives that crown, “not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.”

In this last battle Israel cannot lose so long as we keep the commandments, have faith in Christ, and endure to the end. But if we stay in sin, we die with the heathen.

precepts.text: Preach the word in season and out; the time comes when men will not endure sound doctrine.
precepts.point: Ahab said there was one man, Micaiah, but he hated him because he never prophesied good, only evil, meaning he told the truth.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 18: Jehoshaphat, Ahab, and the True Prophet

precepts.why:
“Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all longsuffering and doctrine.”

“For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears; And they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables.”

That was Ahab. He had heaped to himself prophets that told him what he wanted to hear, and he hated the one man who spoke the truth: “he never prophesied good unto me, but always evil.”

precepts.text: Only Luke is with me, take Mark; Luke traveled with Paul, and Mark is the one who wrote the Gospel of Mark.
precepts.point: Theophilus' name means love of God. He was an Israelite, not a gentile, and Luke addresses him as "most excellent," a title of nobility or government office, the same way Paul addressed "most noble Festus."

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with thee: for he is profitable to me for the ministry.”

Luke traveled with Paul. When others had gone, Luke was still with him. And the Mark Paul calls for is the one who wrote the Gospel of Mark. These were the men under the apostles, the ones the teaching was passed down to, and that is how Luke came to write his former treatise and then the Acts.

precepts.point: Paul warns in 1 Corinthians 9:27 that he keeps his body under subjection lest he himself become a castaway.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Titus was one of those drawn away by this false doctrine. He eventually forsook Paul: “For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus unto Dalmatia.”

The same Titus who stood with Paul in Jerusalem and was not compelled to be circumcised later fell away through these doctrines about circumcision and animal sacrifice. If Titus could fall, anybody could fall.
